capsuleTopic.title: Sermon on the Mount
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Blessing · law · prayer · trust · judgment · doing
capsuleTopic.orientation: Enter the complete mountain discourse from the gathered crowds and opening blessings through law, hidden devotion, trust, judgment, doing, distinct Lukan parallels, and later canonical reuse.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Notice whom Jesus addresses, what each saying observes or commands, which outcomes are promised or warned, how one section qualifies another, and what the discourse leaves unresolved.

passages.title: The poor, Kingdom, neighbor love, and mercy meet judgment
passages.excerpt: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.  For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes…
passages.observation: James prohibits partiality and says God chose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom.

payload.description: Crowds gather, Jesus sits with disciples, and the opening blessings name people whose present condition and promised future do not look alike.

nodes.note: Jesus teaches in Galilee, announces the Kingdom, heals disease, and becomes known across a wide region.
nodes.title: Teaching, healing, and crowds gather before the mountain

nodes.note: Seeing the crowds, Jesus goes up the mountain, sits, and receives his disciples.
nodes.title: Jesus sits and begins to teach

nodes.note: Jesus calls the poor in spirit blessed.
nodes.title: The poor in spirit receive the Kingdom

nodes.note: Jesus calls those who mourn blessed.
nodes.title: Those who mourn will be comforted

nodes.note: Jesus calls the gentle blessed.
nodes.title: The gentle will inherit the earth

nodes.note: Jesus calls those who hunger and thirst for righteousness blessed.
nodes.title: Hunger for righteousness will be filled

nodes.note: Jesus calls the merciful blessed.
nodes.title: The merciful will receive mercy

nodes.note: Jesus calls the pure in heart blessed.
nodes.title: The pure in heart will see God

nodes.note: Jesus calls peacemakers blessed.
nodes.title: Peacemakers will be called God’s children

nodes.note: Jesus calls people persecuted for righteousness and for his sake blessed.
nodes.title: Persecution is joined to Kingdom and joy

nodes.note: Jesus calls the hearers the earth’s salt and the world’s light, warning about salt that loses its function and light that is hidden.
nodes.title: Salt, light, and visible works

payload.title: The mountain and those called blessed

payload.description: The discourse closes through judgment, discernment, asking, two ways, fruit, profession, obedience, foundations, and the crowd’s response to authority.

nodes.note: Jesus warns against judging because measure returns to the one who measures and contrasts another’s speck with one’s own beam.
nodes.title: Judgment begins with the beam in one’s own eye

nodes.note: Jesus warns against giving what is holy to dogs or throwing pearls before pigs.
nodes.title: Holy things and pearls require discernment

nodes.note: Jesus commands asking, seeking, and knocking and states that each receives a corresponding result.
nodes.title: Asking is grounded in the Father’s goodness

nodes.note: Jesus tells hearers to do to others what they desire others to do to them.
nodes.title: The law and prophets are gathered into reciprocal action

nodes.note: Jesus commands entry through the narrow gate and contrasts broad and restricted ways.
nodes.title: Two gates lead toward destruction and life

nodes.note: Jesus warns about false prophets whose outward appearance hides predatory character.
nodes.title: False prophets are known by fruit

nodes.note: Jesus says not everyone calling him Lord enters the Kingdom, but the one doing his Father’s will does.
nodes.title: Speaking and mighty works do not replace being known

nodes.note: Jesus compares everyone hearing and doing his words to a wise builder on rock.
nodes.title: Hearing and doing determine the foundation

nodes.note: Matthew reports that Jesus finishes the sayings and the crowds are astonished.
nodes.title: The crowds respond to Jesus’ authority

nodes.note: Jesus comes down from the mountain with crowds following, and a leper asks to be cleansed if Jesus wills.
nodes.title: Jesus descends and a leper approaches

payload.title: Judgment, discernment, and doing

payload.description: Jesus denies abolishing the law and prophets, then carries murder, adultery, divorce, vows, retaliation, and neighbor love into speech, desire, action, and relationship.

nodes.note: Jesus denies coming to destroy the law or prophets and says he came to fulfill.
nodes.title: Jesus speaks of fulfilling law and prophets

nodes.note: Jesus recalls the murder command and extends danger of judgment to anger and contemptuous speech.
nodes.title: Murder language reaches anger, speech, and reconciliation

nodes.note: Jesus recalls the adultery command and locates adultery in a gaze directed toward lust.
nodes.title: Adultery language reaches the desiring gaze

nodes.note: Jesus recalls the requirement of a divorce writing and speaks about putting away a wife.
nodes.title: A divorce writing is set beside resulting adultery

nodes.note: Jesus recalls commands about vows and says not to swear by heaven, earth, Jerusalem, or one’s head.
nodes.title: Vows give way to unadorned yes and no

nodes.note: Jesus recalls eye-for-eye language and answers injury, lawsuit, forced labor, requests, and borrowing with surprising actions.
nodes.title: Measured retaliation gives way to costly nonresistance

nodes.note: Jesus recalls neighbor love and the saying to hate an enemy, then commands love, blessing, good, and prayer toward enemies and persecutors.
nodes.title: Enemy love is grounded in the Father’s generosity

payload.title: Law, righteousness, and the inner life

payload.description: Luke preserves a distinct level-place discourse and later settings for prayer, asking, provision, and treasure.

nodes.note: Jesus stands on a level place among disciples and a crowd, heals, and addresses the poor, hungry, weeping, and rejected.
nodes.title: Luke places blessings and woes on a level place

nodes.note: Jesus commands love, good, blessing, prayer, nonretaliation, giving, and lending toward enemies.
nodes.title: Luke ends enemy love with the Father’s mercy

nodes.note: Jesus links judging, condemning, releasing, and giving to reciprocal outcomes, then speaks of blind guides and beams.
nodes.title: Judgment, measure, blindness, and fruit form one sequence

nodes.note: Jesus asks why people call him Lord without doing what he says.
nodes.title: Luke’s builders dig deep or lack a foundation

nodes.note: After Jesus prays, a disciple asks to be taught, and Jesus gives a shorter prayer with sins and debts language.
nodes.title: A disciple’s request opens prayer and persistent asking

nodes.note: Jesus tells disciples not to be anxious and directs them to ravens and lilies.
nodes.title: Ravens, lilies, Kingdom, and treasure address fear

payload.title: Teachings in other settings

payload.description: Sinai, commandments, neighbor love, the two ways, and later apostolic instruction create evidence-grounded relationships without erasing each passage’s own setting.

nodes.note: Thunder, cloud, trumpet, fire, and shaking accompany the LORD’s descent on Sinai and Moses’ ascent.
nodes.title: A mountain, gathered people, and a voice at Sinai

nodes.note: God speaks commandments concerning worship, name, Sabbath, family, murder, adultery, theft, witness, and desire.
nodes.title: God speaks commandments and the people stand back

nodes.note: The LORD forbids theft, deception, false swearing, oppression, injustice, slander, hatred, vengeance, and grudges.
nodes.title: Truth, judgment, inner hatred, and neighbor love stand together

nodes.note: The psalm calls one person blessed for rejecting wicked counsel and delighting in the LORD’s law.
nodes.title: Blessing opens into two ways and two outcomes

nodes.note: Paul commands blessing persecutors, sharing joy and grief, humility, peace, and refusal of retaliation.
nodes.title: Blessing persecutors and feeding enemies

nodes.note: James contrasts human anger with God’s righteousness and calls hearers to receive the implanted word.
nodes.title: Anger, hearing, doing, and the law of freedom

nodes.note: James prohibits partiality and says God chose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom.
nodes.title: The poor, Kingdom, neighbor love, and mercy meet judgment

payload.title: Earlier words and later echoes

payload.description: Giving, prayer, forgiveness, and fasting are inspected through audience, motive, hidden practice, and the Father who knows and sees.

nodes.note: Jesus warns against doing merciful deeds before people in order to be seen.
nodes.title: Giving is tested by its audience

nodes.note: Jesus contrasts prayer for public notice with prayer behind a closed door and warns against vain repetition.
nodes.title: Prayer is separated from display and many words

nodes.note: Jesus teaches prayer addressed to “Our Father,” moving through God’s name, Kingdom, will, bread, debts, temptation, and evil.
nodes.title: The disciples are given a shared prayer

nodes.note: Jesus states that forgiving people’s trespasses is followed by the Father’s forgiveness.
nodes.title: Forgiving others is placed beside the Father’s forgiveness

nodes.note: Jesus warns against altering appearance so people notice a fast.
nodes.title: Fasting is hidden from the public gaze

payload.title: The Father who sees in secret

payload.description: Treasure and sight lead into divided service, daily provision, anxiety, value, Kingdom seeking, and the limit of tomorrow.

nodes.note: Jesus contrasts vulnerable earthly treasure with treasure in heaven.
nodes.title: Treasure locates the heart

nodes.note: Jesus calls the eye the body’s lamp and contrasts a sound eye with an evil eye.
nodes.title: The eye fills the body with light or darkness

nodes.note: Jesus states that no one can serve two masters.
nodes.title: God and Mammon cannot both be served

nodes.note: Jesus says not to be anxious about food, drink, body, or clothing and directs attention to birds and lilies.
nodes.title: Life, birds, lilies, and little faith answer anxiety

nodes.note: Jesus repeats the warning against anxious questions about necessities and contrasts the nations’ seeking with the Father’s knowledge.
nodes.title: Kingdom seeking is placed before tomorrow

payload.title: Treasure, service, and tomorrow
